facts.text: La Grange was founded in 1827 when Oldham County’s seat moved from Westport at Major William Berry Taylor’s suggestion.
The town was named after Château de la Grange‑Bléneau, the French estate of Marquis de Lafayette, who visited in 1824.
Main Street in La Grange carries a CSX street‑running mainline where freight trains share the road with local traffic.
The La Grange Railroad Museum sits beside the active tracks, showcasing vintage cars, a dining car, and a caboose once owned by the Louisville & Nashville Railroad.
The Oldham County History Center near Springs Park offers guided tours that explore the area’s Civil War significance and early settler stories.
